MCX recorded a record daily turnover of Rs 62.93 lakh crore on August 28, driven by a sharp surge in options trading and rising participation in commodity derivatives.
August 29, 2026 / 18:26 IST
MCX daily turnover hits record Rs 62.93 lakh crore as commodity derivatives trading surges
The Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) recorded an all-time high daily turnover of Rs 62.93 lakh crore on August 28, up 172% from its previous record of Rs 23.13 lakh crore in November 2025, as trading activity in commodity derivatives continued to expand.
The exchange recorded more than 3.13 crore futures and options contracts on the day. Options accounted for Rs 61.85 lakh crore of the turnover, while futures contributed Rs 1.09 lakh crore. MCX reports options turnover on a notional basis.
The record comes after a sharp rise in activity during the current financial year. MCX's average daily futures and options turnover rose 145% year-on-year to Rs 5.4 lakh crore in FY26, according to its full-year results.
In the April-June quarter of FY27, average daily F&O turnover rose further, with options activity accounting for much of the increase. Options average daily notional turnover rose 266% year-on-year to Rs 9.9 lakh crore, while combined F&O average daily turnover rose 238% to Rs 10.5 lakh crore.
The August 28 record, however, was far above those daily averages, with options accounting for more than 98% of the day's reported F&O turnover.
“The record turnover reflects the growing depth and participation in India’s commodity derivatives market. As more participants use exchange-traded products for price discovery and risk management, such volumes are an encouraging indication of the market’s evolution,” said Rajeev Agarwal, national president of the Commodity & Capital Market Participants Association of India.
He said the focus going forward should remain on broadening participation while maintaining transparency and strong risk-management standards.
Earlier this year, MCX introduced Good Delivery Norms for primary aluminium, refined copper and refined zinc, setting standards for empanelment of producing plants and acceptance of metal for delivery against exchange contracts.
The framework includes auditing, assaying and testing at producing plants.
“The rise in participation on MCX demonstrates the increasing relevance of organised commodity markets for hedgers, traders and investors,” said Naveen Mathur, commodities market expert and director—commodities, currencies and GIFT City, IFSC at Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers.
He said measures that strengthen the link between physical and derivatives markets, including standardised delivery and quality frameworks, add credibility to the ecosystem.
